style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: A morning prayer -- 'in the morning You hear my voice; in the morning I set my case in order before You and keep watch' -- from a man who begins the day surrounded by liars and ends it under a shield. The psalm alternates between the two kinds of people who stand before God. The wicked cannot: You are not a God who takes pleasure in wickedness; evil cannot lodge with You; the arrogant do not stand in Your sight; You hate every worker of iniquity and abhor the man of blood and deceit. David, by contrast, comes in -- but only 'by the abundance of Your covenant love,' bowing toward the holy temple in awe. He asks for a straight road because of the men watching for him to stumble, and then describes them with the anatomy Paul borrowed for Romans 3: nothing trustworthy in their mouth, ruin inside, a throat like an open grave, a tongue that flatters. The verdict he asks for is that they fall by their own schemes. The close is for the other company: let all who take refuge in You rejoice and sing forever, because You cover them; You bless the righteous and surround him with favor like a full-length shield.

1.text: For the choir director, for the flutes. A psalm of David. Give ear to my words, O LORD; consider my sighing.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] upon Nehiloth [nechilah -- flutes], A Psalm [mizmor] of David. Give ear [azan] to my words [emer], O LORD [YHWH], consider [bin -- discern] my meditation [hagig -- murmuring, sighing].
1.notes: Two levels of prayer: amarai (H561), the words, and hagigi (H1901), the murmur underneath the words -- the sigh that has not made it into sentences. haazinah and binah (H238, H995): God asked to hear the one and discern the other. Romans 8:26 is the theology of hagig.

2.text: Listen to the sound of my cry for help, my King and my God, for it is to You that I pray.
2.amp: Hearken [qashab -- attend closely] unto the voice [qol] of my cry [sheva -- cry for help], my King [melek] and my God [Elohim]: for unto You will I pray [palal].
2.notes: malki v-Elohai (H4428, H430) -- my King and my God: David the king addressing his King; the throne is not the top of the chain. shavi (H7773) is the alarm-cry, and palal (H6419) the prayer-verb: elekha etpallal, to YOU -- not to the court, not to the army.

3.text: O LORD, in the morning You will hear my voice; in the morning I will set my case in order before You, and keep watch.
3.amp: My voice [qol] shall You hear [shama] in the morning [boqer], O LORD [YHWH]; in the morning will I direct [arak -- arrange, set in order] my prayer unto You, and will look up [tsaphah -- keep watch, as a watchman].
3.notes: boqer twice (H1242): the day's first act. arak (H6186) is the verb for laying the wood on the altar and arranging troops for battle -- prayer set out in order like an offering or a battle line -- and tsaphah (H6822), the watchman's verb: having laid it out, he climbs the tower and watches for the answer (cf. Habakkuk 2:1).

4.text: For You are not a God who takes pleasure in wickedness; evil cannot be Your guest.
4.amp: For You are not a God [El] that has pleasure [chaphets] in wickedness [resha]: neither shall evil [ra] dwell [gur -- sojourn, lodge as a guest] with You.
4.notes: lo El-chaphets resha attah (H410, H2655, H7562): not a God who delights in wickedness -- the ground of the whole psalm. lo yegurkha ra (H1481, H7451): evil cannot even gur, sojourn, take a room, in Your presence. Holiness stated as the limit of hospitality.

5.text: The boastful cannot take their stand before Your eyes; You hate all who work iniquity.
5.amp: The foolish [holel -- the boastful, the arrogant] shall not stand [yatsab -- take a stand] in Your sight ['before thine eyes', ayin, the KJV margin]: You hate [sane] all workers [paal] of iniquity [aven].
5.notes: holelim (H1984): filed under the same Strong's number as halal, praise -- the self-praisers, the boasters (whether one root or a homonym, the lexicons differ) -- lo-yityatsevu le-neged enekha (H3320, H5869), cannot hold their ground before Your eyes. saneta kol-poale aven (H8130, H6466, H205): a hatred the Psalms do not soften; God's love is not indifference to what destroys.

6.text: You destroy those who speak lies; the LORD abhors the man of blood and deceit.
6.amp: You shall destroy [abad] them that speak [dabar] leasing [kazab -- lies]: the LORD [YHWH] will abhor [taab] the bloody ['man of bloods and deceit', the KJV margin] and deceitful [mirmah] man [ish].
6.notes: dovere kazab (H1696, H3577), the lie-speakers, abad (H6) -- and ish-damim u-mirmah (H376, H1818, H4820), the man of bloods and fraud, whom YHWH yetaeb (H8581), abhors as a thing that turns the stomach. Violence and deceit are paired throughout the Psalms as the two hands of the same man.

7.text: But I -- by the abundance of Your covenant love I will come into Your house; in awe of You I will bow down toward Your holy temple.
7.amp: But as for me, I will come [bo] into Your house [bayith] in the multitude [rob -- abundance] of Your mercy [chesed -- covenant love]: and in Your fear [yirah -- reverence] will I worship [shachah -- bow low] toward Your holy ['the temple of thy holiness', qodesh, the KJV margin] temple [hekal].
7.notes: va-ani -- and I: the contrast. David comes in where the wicked cannot stand -- but be-rob chasdekha (H7230, H2617), by the abundance of YOUR covenant love, not by his own standing; and be-yiratekha (H3374), in awe. Access is grace-funded and reverence-shaped. hekal qodshekha (H1964, H6944): the tent-sanctuary of David's day already called a palace-temple.

8.text: Lead me, O LORD, in Your righteousness, because of those who lie in wait for me; make Your road straight before my face.
8.amp: Lead [nachah] me, O LORD [YHWH], in Your righteousness [tsedaqah] because of mine enemies ['those which observe me', shorer -- the watchers, the KJV margin]; make Your way [derek] straight [yashar] before my face [panim].
8.notes: nechani (H5148), the shepherd-verb of Psalm 23:3 -- be-tsidqatekha (H6666), in Your righteousness -- le-maan shorerai (H8324), because of my WATCHERS, the margin's word: enemies whose weapon is waiting for a stumble. hayshar le-phanai darkekha (H3474, H6440, H1870): a straight road is the answer to men hoping you trip.

9.text: For there is nothing trustworthy in their mouth; their inward parts are pure ruin; their throat is an open grave; with their tongue they flatter smooth.
9.amp: For there is no faithfulness ['stedfastness', kun, the KJV margin] in their mouth ['his mouth, that is, the mouth of any of them', peh]; their inward part [qereb] is very wickedness ['wickednesses', havvah -- ruin, craving]; their throat [garon] is an open [pathach] sepulchre [qeber -- grave]; they flatter [chalaq -- make smooth] with their tongue [lashon].
9.notes: The anatomy Paul borrows for Romans 3:13: en be-phihu nekhonah (H6310, H3559), nothing firm in the mouth; qirbam havvot (H7130, H1942), the insides are ruin; qeber-patuach geronam (H6913, H6605, H1627), the throat an open grave -- speech that smells of death; leshonam yachaliqun (H3956, H2505), the tongue makes things smooth. From the lungs out, a corpse dressed as a courtier.

10.text: Hold them guilty, O God; let them fall by their own schemes; drive them out for the mass of their transgressions, for they have rebelled against You.
10.amp: Destroy ['Make them guilty', asham, the KJV margin] You them, O God [Elohim]; let them fall [naphal] by ['from', the KJV margin] their own counsels [moetsah -- schemes]; cast them out [nadach] in the multitude [rob] of their transgressions [pesha]; for they have rebelled [marah] against You.
10.notes: haashimem (H816): the margin has it -- declare them guilty, the verdict-verb -- and the sentence is poetic justice: yippelu mi-moatsotehem (H5307, H4156), fall by their own schemes, Haman's gallows (cf. Esther 7:10). be-rob pishehem (H7230, H6588) balances verse 7's be-rob chasdekha: abundance of transgression against abundance of covenant love. ki-maru bakh (H4784): the rebellion was, in the end, against God.

11.text: But let all who take refuge in You rejoice; let them shout for joy forever, because You spread Your cover over them; let those who love Your name exult in You.
11.amp: But let all those that put their trust [chasah -- take refuge] in You rejoice [samach]: let them ever [olam] shout for joy [ranan], because You defend ['coverest over, or, protectest them', sakak -- screen, hedge in, the KJV margin] them: let them also that love [ahab] Your name [shem] be joyful [alats -- exult] in You.
11.notes: The other company: kol-chose bakh (H2620) -- everyone taking refuge -- yismechu, le-olam yerannenu (H8055, H5769, H7442). The reason is sakak (H5526), the verb of the cherubim's wings over the mercy seat (cf. Exodus 25:20): You screen them. ohave shemekha (H157, H8034) yaaletsu (H5970): love of the Name produces exultation.

12.text: For You, O LORD, bless the righteous; You wrap him in favor like a full-length shield.
12.amp: For You, LORD [YHWH], will bless [barak] the righteous [tsaddiq]; with favour [ratson] will You compass ['crown', atar -- encircle, the KJV margin] him as with a shield [tsinnah -- the large body-shield].
12.notes: tevarekh tsaddiq (H1288, H6662) -- and the last image: ka-tsinnah ratson taterennu (H6793, H7522, H5849). The tsinnah is the door-sized shield a bearer carried ahead of a warrior, not the small buckler; and atar is 'crown, encircle' -- favor as armor that surrounds the whole man. The morning that began under watching enemies ends behind a wall of goodwill.
